## Paper

The Theory of Industrial Organization

pricing_arena

## Institution

Pricing game baseline with no regulatory institution.

## Agent type

Strategic firms / pricing agents.

## Theoretical benchmark

Static Bertrand/Nash pricing and joint-profit/collusive price benchmarks.

## Learning setup

Repeated duopoly pricing with learned policies compared against static one-shot references.

## Metrics

Average price, welfare/profit, Nash and joint-profit benchmark gaps, price/profit collusion indices.

## Main result

The book provides a comprehensive analysis of industrial organization, including topics such as monopoly power, product selection, pricing behavior, and dynamic price competition.

## What they prove

Do not cite this extracted card for a specific theorem without checking the relevant chapter/pages. In this repo, the source is used as an industrial-organization theory anchor for Nash/Bertrand and joint-profit reference concepts.

## What they do NOT test

Learning pricing agents, deep-RL/MARL capability ladders, exploitability protocols, and institution sweeps in this repo's discrete repeated-pricing environment.

## What we need to reproduce

Reproduce the IO benchmark role: every Pricing Arena result needs Nash/Bertrand and joint-profit reference lines before learned prices are interpreted.

## How our project differs

The book gives classical theory; the repo tests learned behavior under repeated interaction and institutions. Theory is the reference scale, not a claim that agents solve the static model.

## Implementation obligations

Compute static Nash price pairs; compute symmetric joint-profit price; expose benchmark columns in summaries; distinguish competitive benchmark from collusive benchmark.
